doc: Renderer settings (dgVoodoo2 DirectX wrapper + game options). One row = one setting written by the launcher.

rows.purpose: fill a widescreen monitor with the 4:3 game picture (player's choice: no bars, slight horizontal stretch)
dgVoodoo owns the screen mode (game hangs at 'Loading' when it switches modes itself)
rows.verified: yes: needed, or the game hangs at Loading

rows.purpose: enumerate the 4:3 mode at desktop height (e.g. 1440x1080); widescreen breaks the game's 4:3 culling (units/buildings vanish when panning)
rows.verified: yes: at 1440x1080 nothing disappears when panning (player test)

rows.purpose: room for HD textures. 2000 broke creature textures even with original art (Netherfiend black, Phoenix/Silverback wings): the 2001 engine mishandles that much video memory -> back to 1024
start unelevated with Windows 2000 heap/compat shims (XP layers force elevation; plain layer crashes in ntdll heap)
rows.verified: yes: Win2000 layer + dinputto8 stops the startup crash

rows.purpose: Bigger draw distance: highest Graphic detail (0 = most detail; matches a maxed-out install)
full-resolution character textures (9 = top of the slider)
stop the engine's automatic detail reduction from hiding units, souls and far terrain while the camera moves
keep the game at 60 fps: above 60 the computer players stand still at the start of a match (known engine issue on modern PCs)
render the 3D scene at twice the game resolution and scale down (supersampling): sharper creatures and finer edges without touching their textures
per-pixel lighting: smoother shading on low-poly creatures and models
sharper scaling of the final picture to the screen
